title: Song of Solomon Bible Quiz - Chapter 5
description: Ten questions on Song of Solomon 5: the beloved at the door, the search through the city, and the bride's description of her beloved, the best among ten thousand.

questions.text: What does the beloved say he has eaten in his garden?
questions.explanation: He says, "I have come into my garden... I have eaten my honeycomb with my honey; I have drunk my wine with my milk."

answers.text: His figs with his raisins
His honeycomb with his honey
His bread with his oil
His apples with his pomegranates

questions.text: Why does the beloved who knocks say, "Open to me"?
questions.explanation: He says, "Open to me, my sister, my love, my dove, my undefiled; for my head is filled with dew, and my hair with the dampness of the night."

answers.text: Because the watchmen are pursuing him
Because the night is dark and cold
Because he has brought her precious fruits
Because his head is filled with dew

questions.text: What reasons does the speaker give for hesitating to open the door?
questions.explanation: She says, "I have taken off my robe. Indeed, must I put it on? I have washed my feet. Indeed, must I soil them?"

answers.text: She has taken off her robe and washed her feet
She is afraid of the watchmen in the street
She has locked the door for the night
Her mother's house is shut for the night

questions.text: What dripped from the speaker's hands when she rose to open for her beloved?
questions.explanation: She says, "My hands dripped with myrrh, my fingers with liquid myrrh, on the handles of the lock."

answers.text: Oil
Honey
Myrrh
Perfumed water

questions.text: What did the speaker find when she opened to her beloved?
questions.explanation: She opened to her beloved, but her beloved had left and gone away; she looked for him but didn't find him, called him but he didn't answer.

answers.text: He stood behind the wall, glancing through the lattice
He had left and gone away
He was waiting with the daughters of Jerusalem
He was asleep at the door

questions.text: What did the watchmen who go about the city do to the speaker?
questions.explanation: The watchmen found her, beat her, and bruised her, and the keepers of the walls took her cloak away from her.

answers.text: They led her to her beloved
They asked her where her beloved had gone
They shut her outside the city gates
They beat her, bruised her, and took her cloak away

questions.text: What does the speaker want the daughters of Jerusalem to tell her beloved if they find him?
questions.explanation: She adjures them, if they find her beloved, to tell him that she is faint with love.

answers.text: That she is faint with love
That she waits in her mother's house
That the watchmen have beaten her
That the door now stands open

questions.text: Complete the speaker's words: "My beloved is white and ruddy. The best among..."
questions.explanation: She says, "My beloved is white and ruddy. The best among ten thousand."

answers.text: a thousand
all the sons
ten thousand
the mighty men

questions.text: How is the beloved's hair described?
questions.explanation: She says, "His head is like the purest gold. His hair is bushy, black as a raven."

answers.text: White as wool
Like a flock of goats
Like purple tresses
Bushy, black as a raven

questions.text: What are the beloved's legs compared to?
questions.explanation: She says, "His legs are like pillars of marble set on sockets of fine gold."

answers.text: Cedars of Lebanon
Pillars of marble
Towers of ivory
Rings of gold set with beryl
